threads.body: `applyTo` is a single quoted string containing commas, so it will be treated as one glob pattern (including the commas). Since repo paths won’t contain commas, this likely won’t match anything and the rubric won’t auto-apply. Consider switching to a YAML list of globs (or otherwise using the supported multi-pattern syntax) so it applies to `model/**`, `docs/gen-ai/**`, and `reference/scenarios/**` as intended.
threads.hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+---
+description: "Rubric for evaluating whether semantic-convention changes are supported by reference scenarios."
+applyTo: "model/**,docs/gen-ai/**,reference/scenarios/**"

replies.body:
Declining. The comma-separated single-string syntax is the documented form per [GitHub's official docs on path-specific custom instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/add-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions#creating-path-specific-custom-instructions):

> You can specify multiple patterns by separating them with commas. For example, to apply the instructions to all TypeScript files in the repository, you could use the following frontmatter block:
> ```
> ---
> applyTo: "**/*.ts,**/*.tsx"
> ---
> ```

A YAML list form is not documented anywhere in the official Copilot docs, so switching to one would not be a supported syntax.
